practice.mastery[0]: The booklet does not ask students to recover an unseen intercept from a partial graph and a visible vertex. Its symmetry statement is teaching, not this question type; replace this item with a same-tier adaptation of an explicit graph-feature question.

practice.mastery[1]: The booklet does not ask students to diagnose confusion between vertex coordinates and the axis equation. Replace this item with a same-tier graph-feature question; the explanation-of-error questions elsewhere assess different tasks.

practice.mastery[2]: Reading the features is supported by Development 3, lines 389–444. The additional request to show numerically that the axis lies midway between the intercepts is not an explicit booklet question type: lines 547–549 ask why symmetry gives that relationship. Remove or repair that additional demand.

theory: Define intercepts as points where the curve meets an axis, including touching it; 'crosses' excludes the single-intercept cases explicitly assessed in Foundation 2(b,d), lines 355–380. Make the midpoint step conditional on two distinct $x$-intercepts and explain that otherwise the axis passes vertically through the vertex; the current unconditional procedure fails for the supplied one-intercept and no-intercept graphs.
summary: Replaced the two unsupported Mastery tasks with cited graph-feature questions using new values, and removed the additional numerical symmetry demand from the third without removing any whole item. Corrected the intercept definitions and conditional axis procedure, updated affected solution headings, and preserved all other content and quiz questions.
reviewSummary: All 24 items have correct answers, appropriate graph-reading methods and supported booklet question types; every quiz has exactly one correct option with accurate distractor explanations. The theory is consistent with the booklet, no worked examples were supplied, and no removals were proposed.
